correctness.rationale: The full proof uses Cayley--Hamilton for Witt involutions; the split semidirect product with trace-zero kernel; classification of characteristic-two SL2 involutions by a unique projective fixed line; exact two-dimensional adjoint fixed spaces; and exhaustive logical case distinctions for all commuting pairs and maximal cliques. The q-dependent incidence and spectrum formulas follow by disjoint counting. The independent arithmetic implementation enumerated all special-linear elements in both ring models at q=2,4 and confirmed all four count/graph predictions. Finite checks support but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The new result is the complete projective-line maximal-elementary-abelian-subgroup incidence model and involution commuting spectrum for the pair of length-two SL2 groups. Stasinski proves the degree equality and a no-lift fact in the Witt group; these known pieces are acknowledged and do not by themselves specify all maximal cliques, intersection sizes and three-stratum commuting frequencies of the split group. Inspected articles on commuting-involution graphs study different field groups. Public and accessible own-claim searches yielded no asserted implication covering this entire classification; priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: A full classification of maximal elementary abelian 2-subgroups and intersection geometry, plus the exact involution commuting graph and partner-count spectrum, are natural complete invariants of these finite linear groups. They sharply distinguish groups known from Stasinski to have the same complete irreducible character-degree distribution, and determine different Frobenius--Schur indicator-weighted sums. The projective-line incidence description and all-field quantifiers provide genuine structural value beyond a single exceptional matrix or a small count.
